 Follow us on Facebook Twitter Hello NFL Scores Standings Schedule Super Bowl Draft AFC NFC NFL Jon Gruden rips Los Angeles Chargers and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel
 The Los Angeles Chargers are the only winless team in the NFL almost halfway through the season, and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is in the hot seat.
 SEAN M. HAFFEY Dane Arlauckas twitter Update: Nov 7th, 2026 15:54 EST 0 Share facebook twitter whatsapp Make us preferred on Google The Los Angeles Chargers are quite literally the worst team in football. They are the only winless team in the league, and it seems like everyone is lining up to take their shot at the LA, coach Jim Harbaugh and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. 
 Gruden roasts McDaniel 
 Super Bowl winning coach Jon Gruden is the latest to give his brutal take on the Chargers, and what has been a dormant offense over the last three games. While talking on Draft Kings’ Jon Gruden Family Football show, the former Raiders coach put Mike McDaniel in the crosshairs essentially blaming him for the Chargers problems. 
 View this post on Instagram 
 When he was asked who he was taking in the Chargers upcoming game against the Houston Texans, Gruden said, “I just can’t got with the Chargers. They haven’t scored a touchdown in 27 possession. The longest streak since the Dolphins went 30 possessions. I think the offensive coordinator was the coach coach of the Dolphins.”
 The last touchdown the Chargers scored came on October 11th. They have gone nearly a month without getting in the end zone since Kimani Vidal took a 42 yard run to the end zone against the Denver Broncos. Since then they have gone seven quarters without scoring a touchdowns, and dropped to 0-7. 
 McDaniel “compromising” Herbert 
 Then Grunden went deeper into some of the problems their quarterback, Justin Herbert could be having under McDaniel. “I call it compromising ball handling. When your Justin Herbert, and you have to fake a hand off over here, and then spin around over here, and then read the defense from there to there. I don’t know what these plays are. I don’t like the Chargers right now. I’m going to take the Texans, 13-10.”
 View this post on Instagram 
 McDaniel was supposed to bring the best out of what has been a constantly underachieving Chargers offense.They went 11-6 in each of their last two seasons under Jim Harbaugh. Their offense fluttered towards the end of those seasons, and Greg Roman was replaced with former Miami Dolphins coach Mike McDaniel. He was supposed to be the offensive wizard who was going to unlock Herbert’s full potential. Heading into Week 9, the Chargers are essentially out of the playoff hunt, and McDaniel is clinging to his job. 
 Coming out of the University of Oregon, Herbert was almost automatically put in the upper class of quarterbacks in the league, but since 2020 he has led the Chargers to three playoff appearances and is still looking for his first playoff win. He had 4,000 yard seasons in each of his first three years, but has struggled since, and this year is averaging less than 200 yards passing per game, with five touchdowns and a league high 10 interceptions.
